description: A Guide to Assessing Green Infrastructure Costs and Benefits for Flood Reduction is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA Office for Coastal Management. Communities can use this guide to assess the potential costs and benefits of green infrastructure to reduce flooding. The framework can be adapted to inform planning-scale assessments and spark discussion about green infrastructure options to mitigate flooding and provide other watershed benefits. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – General. Assets: Economy, Energy and Utilities, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
